mcqs.question: Can a single subnet span multiple Availability Zones?
options: Yes, subnets are always region-wide by design
No — a subnet is tied to exactly one Availability Zone
Yes, but only for private subnets
It depends on the VPC's IP address range size
mcqs.explanation: Subnets are AZ-scoped: each one lives in a single AZ, which is why resilient designs create one subnet per tier per AZ rather than a single wide subnet. The VPC itself spans the region; subnets are the AZ-level subdivision.

mcqs.question: A private-subnet app server needs to download OS security patches from the internet, but must never accept unsolicited inbound connections. What's the right setup?
options: Move it to a public subnet with a public IP
Give it a route through a NAT gateway in a public subnet for outbound-only access
Open an inbound rule for HTTPS from 0.0.0.0/0
It cannot reach the internet at all while in a private subnet
mcqs.explanation: A NAT gateway is exactly for this: it lets private-subnet resources initiate outbound connections (like fetching patches) while blocking any inbound connection initiated from outside. Moving it to a public subnet or opening inbound rules would unnecessarily expose it.

mcqs.question: Why is a security group described as 'stateful' while a network ACL is 'stateless'?
options: Security groups remember rule changes across reboots; ACLs don't
A security group auto-allows the return traffic for an allowed request; a network ACL requires you to explicitly allow both the request and its reply
Stateful means it can only allow traffic, never deny it — that's actually true of both
Network ACLs cannot be attached to a VPC at all
mcqs.explanation: Statefulness is about whether the return leg of a connection is automatically permitted. Security groups track connection state and allow the reply automatically; network ACLs evaluate each direction independently, so you must write a rule for both inbound and outbound.

mcqs.question: Your company is about to connect 12 teams' VPCs so every team can reach every other team's services. Why would VPC peering become a poor choice here?
options: VPC peering doesn't support any security rules
Peering connections scale O(N²), so 12 VPCs would need up to 66 separate peering connections to fully connect
VPC peering only works within a single Availability Zone
Peering is deprecated and no longer supported by any provider
mcqs.explanation: Full mesh peering among N VPCs requires N(N-1)/2 connections — 66 for 12 VPCs — which becomes unmanageable. A transit gateway's hub-and-spoke model needs only one connection per VPC (12 total) and adds central routing control.
